title: Orientation, Access, and Growth Playbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook describes the standardized, self-serviceable process for bringing new Redwood engineers and product teammates to productivity, granting safe and timely access to internal systems, and accelerating through the role ladder during the first 12 months. It combines working-at-Redwood cultural guidance, the role-and-career framing used by People Ops and managers, benefits orientation checkpoints, hiring-to-join handoffs, and the internal tools checklist required for production work.

Scope
- Applies to: full-time employees, contractors on >90 day engagements, and interns moving to full-time.
- Not for: short-term vendors (separate vendor onboarding flow in Procurement).

Quick links
- New Hire Portal (People Ops): https://redwood.internal/new-hire
- Access Request Service (Provisioner): https://provisioner.redwood.internal
- IT & Device Ordering: https://it.redwood.internal/devices
- Career Framework: https://confluence.redwood/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career

Core principles
- Empathy first: a measurable first week experience aimed at psychological safety and early wins.
- Self-service: most access and tooling steps are automated via Provisioner and the People Ops portal.
- Transparent expectations: managers provide clear 30/60/90 goals mapped to role proficiency.
- Ownership and escalation: People Ops owns the playbook; engineering managers own daily execution.

Onboarding timeline and checklists (Day 0 -> 90)

Day 0 (Offer accepted -> start date)
1. People Ops: send Welcome Kit and pre-boarding checklist (tax forms, KYC, T&C).
2. Provisioner: auto-create account skeleton on start date, pre-request laptop per role.
3. Manager: assign 1:1 buddy and prepare first-week schedule.

Day 1 (Orientation)
- New hire completes orientation session: company mission, values, benefits overview (medical, retirement, parental leave), and core policies.
- Device pickup or tracking for delivery.
- Access snapshot: Email, Okta SSO, Slack, Confluence, Jira, GitHub (read), CI read-only.

Week 1 (Setup & small wins)
- Complete mandatory security training and SSO MFA setup.
- Join team channel, complete first codebase readme and run local dev image.
- Schedule 1:1 weekly cadence with manager; buddy-led code walkthrough.

30-day goals (baseline proficiency)
- Able to make a small production fix or feature; submit PR and follow the release playbook.
- Demonstrate understanding of the team’s alerting and deployment process.

60-day goals (independent contributor)
- Take ownership of a small service or product area with documented acceptance criteria.
- Start contributing to the team roadmap discussions and retrospectives.

90-day goals (role-aligned impact)
- Deliver a measurable outcome tied to team metrics (latency, cost-per-token, user adoption).
- Completed role calibration conversation with manager and People Ops (optionally request an early stretch assignment).

Role acceleration and laddering (how to progress)
- The Career Framework is organized by competencies (Delivery, Craft, Systemic Impact, Leadership).
- Acceleration levers: documented project outcomes, cross-team collaborations, public technical writings, mentoring others, and measurable product/ops improvements.
- Managers should use the following cadence for promotions/step-ups:
  1) Early calibration at 90 days (informal)
  2) Formal calibration at 6 months (if promoted)
  3) Annual promotion cycle aligning with company review windows

Acceleration metrics (SLOs for ramping)
- Onboarding SLO: 85% of hires should reach 30-day baseline by day 30.
- Full ramp SLO: 70% of hires expected to reach 90-day role-aligned impact by day 90.
- People Ops/Manager escalation if SLOs are missed: open a "New Hire Ramp" ticket within 3 business days.

Access and tools matrix (who provisions what)
| System | Default Access Day | Provisioned By | Escalation Owner | Notes |
|--------|-------------------:|---------------|------------------|-------|
| Email & Okta | Day 0 | People Ops (Provisioner) | IT Ops | SSO enforced; MFA required |
| Slack | Day 0 | Provisioner | Eng Manager | Add to team channel template |
| Confluence (read) | Day 0 | Provisioner | Documentation Team | Page templates added to onboarder space |
| GitHub (read) | Day 1 | Team Admin | Eng Manager | Codeowners added as needed |
| CI/CD (read) | Day 1 | DevOps | Eng SRE | Restricted write access until qualifying tasks complete |
| Production access (staging -> prod) | Post-30 days (role dependent) | Eng Manager + SRE approval | SRE | Requires training and a buddy-verified runbook |

Provisioning examples and CLI snippets
- Quick check of account status (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" https://provisioner.redwood.internal/v1/accounts/me
  Response sample:
  {
    "id": "u-12345",
    "okta_status": "ACTIVE",
    "confluence": "HAS_ACCESS"
  }
- Request a scoped production role (manager approval required):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"user_id":"u-12345","role":"prod-deployer","justification":"owner of service X"}' 
    https://provisioner.redwood.internal/v1/requests

Approval and audit flow
1. All production access requests create an auditable ticket in Jira Access-Requests project.
2. Manager approves increment; SRE confirms runbook competency via checklist.
3. Provisioner calculates least-privilege policy and records grant in audit log for 13 months.

Internal tools orientation (critical first-week tutorials)
- Provisioner walkthrough (15m): request types, SLA expectations, and waiting times.
- CI/CD pipeline tutorial (30m): how to run a canary, rollback, and interpret traces.
- Observability overview (30m): using Dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown per token.
- Cost-awareness primer (20m): how batching, caching, and quantization affect unit economics.

Benefits and perks snapshot (what new hires learn first)
- Health & wellbeing: medical, dental, vision plan summaries, and mental health resources.
- Flex & remote: hybrid-first policy with core collaboration days, office stipend options.
- Leave policies: parental leave, sabbatical eligibility after 3 years, volunteer days.
- Learning & development: $2,500 annual learning stipend, passes to industry conferences, internal mentorship programs.

Hiring -> Offer -> Start handoff checklist (for interviewers & recruiters)
1. Recruiter to People Ops: send signed offer and completed background check.
2. Hiring manager: fill the "First 90-day impact plan" template and list the onboarding buddy.
3. People Ops: create Provisioner pre-reqs and device order.
4. IT: order device and ship with required security image.

Manager playbook: running the first 90 days
1. Pre-start: create first-week schedule and invite buddy.
2. Week 1: focus on introductions, environment setup, and ping-pong pairing.
3. Week 2-4: incremental ownership, codebase orientation, and first PR review goals.
4. 30/60/90 check-ins: fill calibration form and collect manager/buddy feedback.
5. If ramp is delayed: open a New Hire Ramp ticket specifying blockers and mitigation steps.

Templates and required artifacts (links)
- 30/60/90 goal template: https://confluence.redwood/company-handbook/templates/30-60-90
- First 90-day impact plan template: https://confluence.redwood/company-handbook/templates/first-90-impact
- Access request template (manager): https://provisioner.redwood.internal/templates/access-request

Frequently asked questions
Q: What if my laptop arrives late?
A: People Ops provides a short-term loaner or a stipend to co-work from a local Redwood partner space for up to 7 days.

Q: How long until I can deploy to production?
A: Typical path requires passing the team’s runbook checklist and a buddy-verified on-call shadow (usually >= 30 days). Exceptions must be approved by manager + SRE.

Ownership, SLAs, and metrics
- People Ops: maintain playbook and monitor onboarding SLOs.
- Engineering managers: deliver weekly check-ins and role calibration.
- IT/Platform: device fulfillment SLA = 5 business days (target).
- Provisioner: mean time to grant non-sensitive access = 1 business day; production requests = 3 business days (including approvals).

Related pages
- Career Framework overview: https://confluence.redwood/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/career-framework
- New Hire Checklist (detailed): https://confluence.redwood/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/new-hire-checklist

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (Priya Shah).
- Review cadence: annual + triggered by policy changes (security, legal, or benefits programs).
- To propose changes: open an edit request on this page and add the appropriate reviewer(s) from the reviewers list above.

Appendix: quick manager checklist (one-pager)
1. Confirm buddy and schedule orientation on Day 1.
2. Complete the First 90-day impact plan before start.
3. Verify access (Okta, Slack, GitHub) within first 48 hours.
4. Assign initial tasks that produce a small, reviewable artifact.
5. Run 30/60/90 calibration conversations and submit feedback to People Ops.

This playbook is intended to be practical and lightweight. If you find a step that can be automated, file an improvement request with the Provisioner team and include the expected time savings and risk assessment.
